actual_title: Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (Grid Interactive Rooftop Renewable Energy Generating Systems) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2023
actual_doc_number: MERC/Tech/Regulation/2023/0609 (read from the Marathi notification; the English text leaves the number blank as "No. MERC/Tech/Regulation/___")
effective_date_basis_note: Reg. 2.2: "These Regulations shall come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette." Published in Maharashtra Government Gazette Extraordinary Part IV-C, No. 60, Thursday 16 November 2023. The signature block on the last page says "Dated November, 2023" with the day left blank.

status_guess.reason: Still in force. The Second Amendment 2024 (already in the corpus as MH-C3-002) amended it further; it did not repeal it. MERC posted a DRAFT MERC Grid Interactive Rooftop RE Regulations, 2026 in September 2026 (merc.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/3.-Draft-Grid-Interactive-Rooftop-Regulation-2026.pdf). That draft is not yet notified; once notified it would likely replace the 2019 regulations and their amendments.

notes: Bilingual gazette. Pages 1-12 are Marathi; the embedded Devanagari font makes that text extract garbled. Pages 13-23 are English and extract cleanly. Real date: 16 Nov 2023, not 20 Nov 2023. The claimed number MERC/2023/REG-124 does not exist. Substance: this amendment introduces Gross Metering (2.1(k)(a)), the Gross Metering Connection Agreement (2.1(k)(b)), Group Net Metering (2.1(k)(c)) with energy accounting in Reg. 11.9, and Net Billing settlement (Reg. 11(A)). It caps net-metering capacity at 5 MW or contract demand/sanctioned load, whichever is lower. VIRTUAL net metering is NOT in this amendment; it comes from the Second Amendment 2024 (MH-C3-002). So the fabricated excerpt's "Virtual Net Metering" clause is wrong for this instrument. This file does not duplicate MH-C3-002, which is the Second Amendment (29 Aug 2024). Also on merc.gov.in: the Statement of Reasons (…/2023/11/SOR_First-Amendment-to-MERC-Grid-Interactive-RRE-Regulations.pdf) and the SOR for the Second Amendment (…/2024/09/SOR_Second-Amendment.pdf). The Marathi-original Second Amendment gazette is at …/2024/09/Rooftop-Grid-Interactive-RE-Regulations.pdf. Index page: https://merc.gov.in/regulation-detais/merc-grid-interactive-rooftop-renewable-energy-generating-systemfirst-amendment-regulations-2023/

actual_title: MERC Order in Case No. 217 of 2024: MSEDCL Truing-up of ARR for FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24, Provisional Truing-up for FY 2024-25 and approval of ARR and Tariff for FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30 (5th MYT Control Period)
effective_date_basis_note: Para 7.2.1: "The revised Tariff as per this Order shall be applicable from 1 April, 2025." Section 7.33: "Revised Tariff with effect from 1 April, 2025".

status_guess.reason: Its rooftop-solar provisions (ToD slot-wise banking, Grid Support Charges, net-metering treatment) were revisited in MSEDCL review Case No. 75 of 2025: review order about 25 June 2025 (https://www.mahadiscom.in/consumer/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Order_Case-No.75-of-2025.pdf), then a post-remand order dated 25 March 2026. Press reports say the post-remand order activated Grid Support Charges and changed solar banking. Not verified here; those orders were not downloaded.

notes: No MERC "Case No. 182 of 2023" dated 15 Mar 2024 was found. The claimed case and its figures are fabricated, including the "APPC Rs 3.48/kWh annual settlement". The closest real MERC instrument for rooftop banking, settlement and Grid Support Charges in that period is this MSEDCL MYT order. The fabricated excerpt's coram (Sanjay Kumar, Anand M. Limaye, Surendra J. Biyani) matches this order. Relevant pages: 565-583. Section 7.13 covers ToD and net metering: LT-Residential RTS keeps net metering without ToD slot-wise banking restriction (7.13.79-7.13.80), and ToD-slot banking conditions apply to other categories (7.13.93). Section 7.14 covers Grid Support Charges: consumers with sanctioned load up to 10 kW are exempt, and no GSC is levied until state rooftop capacity reaches 5000 MW (7.14.11-7.14.16). 827 pages, 12.9 MB. MSEDCL also hosts a copy at https://www.mahadiscom.in/consumer/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/MSEDCL-MYT-Order_Case_no_217-of-2024.pdf.

actual_title: MERC Order in Case No. 231 of 2023: Petition seeking clarifications on certain provisions in MERC (Grid Interactive Rooftop Renewable Energy Generating Systems) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2023 and MERC (Distribution Open Access) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023
effective_date_basis_note: Clarificatory order, operative from the date of the order (19 May 2025). No separate commencement is stated.

status_guess.reason: No later order superseding these clarifications was found. The banking-charge clarifications may interact with the later tariff orders in Case 217 of 2024 and Case 75 of 2025.

notes: WEAK TOPICAL MATCH. No MERC "Practice Direction No. 04 of 2020" (08 Sep 2020) exists. The MERC orders index lists one rooftop practice direction: "Practice directions under MERC (Net Metering for Roof-top Solar Photo Voltaic Systems) Regulations, 2015", dated 30-09-2016 (https://merc.gov.in/Order-detais/practice-directions-of/). Its attachment link on merc.gov.in is broken (href="Array"), and no other copy was found online. It also sits under the repealed 2015 regulations. As the best retrievable substitute I saved MERC's clarificatory order on implementing the rooftop regulations. It covers: banking charges for HT/LT RTPV; the meaning of "same consumer" for Group Net Metering; priority lists and ratios; GNM settlement; the 50% credit computation; GEOA banking cycle; GEOA for LT; and twelve time blocks. It does NOT cover technical-feasibility timelines or escalation to the CGRF as the fabricated excerpt claims. Please review whether to keep this substitute or record not_found.

actual_title: Guidelines for installations of Roof Top Solar systems under PM SURYA GHAR: Muft Bijli Yojana
actual_issuer: MSEDCL, Office of the Executive Director (Dist-III/Infra)
effective_date_basis_note: No commencement clause. Operative on issue. It directs field officers to comply "before issuing Solar Net Meter".
text_layer: ocr_embedded (Adobe Scan output with vendor OCR layer)

status_guess.reason: PM Surya Ghar runs to FY 2026-27. MSEDCL later supplemented this procedure: RTS Vendor Portal (ED(Infra)/RTS/33498, 22.10.2024), Faceless & Paperless process (ED(Infra)/RTS/34837, 07.11.2024), and others. No revocation was found.

notes: MSEDCL Commercial Circular No. 340 is real but unrelated: it is dated 06.04.2023 and sets the rate of interest on consumer security deposit for FY 2022-23. No MSEDCL "SOP for PM-Surya Ghar" commercial circular exists in the commercial-circulars index (https://www.mahadiscom.in/custom/commercial-circulars.php). MSEDCL issued its PMSG procedure as letters from CE(SPD) and ED(Infra), linked under "Guidelines & Circulars" on the I-SMART rooftop portal (https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/). This 24.07.2024 letter consolidates the PMSG process flow in the New Connection system: auto-processing without vendor selection or registration fee, applications with arrears, auto creation of additional-load applications, auto technical-feasibility approval up to 10 kW, and deemed approval above 10 kW after 15 days. Related letters on the same page: CE(SPD)/RTS/TFR/20949 dt 05.07.2024 (auto approval up to 10 kWp); CE(SPD)/RTS/21347 dt 10.07.2024 (PMSG applications with arrears); CE(SPD)/RTS/21912 dt 16.07.2024 (technical feasibility above 10 kW within the ERoC Amendment Rules 2024 period); ED(Infra)/RTS/34837 dt 07.11.2024 (faceless & paperless). The claimed API push within 2 hours and the 5-day JCR inspection are not in this letter.

actual_title: Guidelines to install solar net meter by AMISP under PMSG: MBY
actual_issuer: MSEDCL, Office of the Executive Director (Dist-III/Infra)
effective_date_basis_note: No commencement clause. It says the instructions are "to be circulated upto field officers immediately".
notes: No MSEDCL "Technical Circular No. 115" (10.09.2024) with IS 16444 four-quadrant smart net meter specifications was found. MSEDCL's testing-circulars index (https://www.mahadiscom.in/custom/testing-circulars.php) has no such item. The published net-meter technical specifications date from 22.01.2016 (https://www.mahadiscom.in/en/consumer/meter-specification-for-net-metering/). The real instrument on solar net meters installed by the AMISP under RDSS/PMSG is this letter. It directs that after the release order on the RTS Vendor portal, the AMISP replaces the old meter with a solar net meter within the set timeline, without waiting for the generation meter. It refers back to CE/SPD/RTS/22336 dt 22.07.2024, the original instruction for MSEDCL to provide and install solar net meters through the AMISP. That letter was not found online.

The claimed Commercial Circular No. 338 is real but unrelated. It is dated 07-09-2022, in Marathi, and amends Circular 337 on the industrial tariff concession for Vidarbha, Marathwada, North Maharashtra and D/D+ areas. No MSEDCL or MERC instrument raising the DT hosting ceiling from 70% to 85% was found. The binding limit is 70% of DT rated capacity: Reg. 5.2 of the MERC Rooftop RE Regulations 2019 (corpus MH-C3-001) and Commercial Circular 322 (corpus MH-C5-001). The MSEDCL "Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Installation & Commissioning of Rooftop Solar System" (undated; PDF created 2022-04-04; https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/media/SoP%20Rooftop%20Solar.pdf) repeats the 70% rule ("D=70% of B- C"). It is a real procedural document if a DT-capacity source is wanted. It was not saved because it does not match the claimed revision.

actual_title: Bulk testing of Generation meters to be utilized for commissioning of RTS installation under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for accelerating progress under said scheme
actual_issuer: MSEDCL, Office of the Executive Director (Dist-III/Infra)
effective_date_basis_note: No commencement clause; operative on issue. The number and date come from a high-resolution re-OCR of the stamped header ("33590", "23 OCT 2024") and match the filename. The embedded text layer garbles the header.
notes: No "MSEDCL/QC/METER/2024/412" (12.11.2024) exists as claimed. The claimed Rs 600 testing fee, 3-day turnaround and holographic seals are not in this instrument. The real instrument allows bulk testing of vendor-procured generation meters for each empanelled vendor, covering 2 months' requirement. Testing happens at Testing Division/O&M Division/Sub-Division benches as directed by the SE; tested meters are marked or stickered for generation-meter use only and used exclusively for PMSG. Pages 3-4 enclose the Ministry of Power letter F. No. 10/05/2022-UR&SI-II (E-263845) dt 17.09.2024. Earlier related letters: CE(Sp.Proj.)/MNRE-Phase-II RTS/No. 21654 dt 18.08.2022 (bulk meter testing for RTS, https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/media/Bulk%20Meter%20testing%20for%20RTS%2021654.pdf) and CE/PMKUSUM B/No. 20038 dt 01.07.2024 (testing of net and generation meters at subdivision/division offices).

actual_title: Commercial Circular No. 334: Guidelines in the matter of RE generators intending to connect their power plants "Behind the meter" as per the provisions of MERC (Grid Interactive Rooftop Renewable Energy Generating Systems) Regulations, 2019
actual_issuer: MSEDCL, Office of the Chief Engineer (Commercial)
actual_doc_number: Commercial Circular No. 334; Ref. CE/Comm/GIRREGS Regulations 2019/06633
effective_date_basis_note: No commencement clause; operative on issue. The date comes from the MSEDCL commercial-circulars index and the filename; the scanned date stamp is illegible in the text layer.

status_guess.reason: Behind-the-meter procedure under the 2019 regulations. MSEDCL letter CE(SPD)/T/RTS/20946 dt 05.07.2024 (multipartite BTM approval) still refers to "the guidelines for behind the meter RTS connection". No revocation found.

notes: The circular number and topic (behind the meter) match the claim, but the date is 17.03.2022, not 14.04.2022. The content also differs from the fabricated excerpt. It contains no gross-metering feed-in tariff and no BESS or anti-islanding provisions. It says: the online application on the RE portal is the prior intimation under Reg. 7.9 and no separate sanction is required; an Electrical Inspector charging permission/certificate is needed; if plant capacity is below 200 kW (the scan renders the comparison sign as "~"), a Licensed Electrical Contractor safety certificate is accepted; HT matters go to the O&M Circle and LT matters to the O&M Subdivision.

actual_title: Authorization of AE(QC) of Subdivision/Division Offices having meter testing facility to test Whole Current Meter and installation up to 20 KW under Roof Top Scheme (RTS), with enclosed Pre-commissioning Testing procedure for AE(QC)
actual_issuer: MSEDCL, Office of the Chief Engineer (Special Projects)
effective_date_basis_note: No commencement clause. The letter says the instructions were already given by Director (Projects) in the RD/CE review meeting dated 10.08.2022. The date is illegible on the scan ("_/8/2022") and was confirmed from the citation in MSEDCL letter CE/PMKUSUM B/No. 20038 dt 01.07.2024 ("CE/Sp.Proj./MNRE-Phase-II RTS/No.21653 dtd.18.08.2022").
text_layer: mixed (page 1 cover letter is an image scan with no text layer and was read here by local OCR; pages 2-11 native text)

status_guess.reason: Reaffirmed and extended to PM Surya Ghar by CE/PMKUSUM B/No. 20038 dt 01.07.2024 (https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/media/Testing%20of%20Rooftop%20solar%20Net%20and%20Generation%20%20Whole%20Current%20Meter%20and%20%20installation%20up%20to%2020%20KW%20at%20%20Subdivision_Division%20Offices.pdf).

notes: No MSEDCL "Technical Circular No. 102" (22.03.2023) with a 10 kVA self-certification / 10-50 kW EE (Testing) / above 50 kW CEI scheme was found. The real MSEDCL instrument on who inspects RTS installations by capacity is this letter. It authorises AE(QC) at subdivision/division level to test whole-current meters and to inspect and release RTS connections up to 20 kW in consultation with the SDO. It encloses a pre-commissioning testing checklist, whose eligibility criterion is "sanctioned load shall be atleast 1 KW but not exceeding 20 KW". The Electrical Inspector threshold in MSEDCL instruments is 200 kW for behind-the-meter systems: Circular 334 (MH-C5-011) and CE(SPD)/T/RTS/20946 dt 05.07.2024 ("obtain the charging permission certificate ... from the concerned Electrical Inspector office in case load>200KW"). A general MSEDCL testing circular on self-certification of MSEDCL's own installations up to 11 kV (notified voltage) under CEA Safety Regs Reg. 30/43 also exists (https://www.mahadiscom.in/consumer/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Inspection-of-Installations-upto-Notified-Voltage-Circular.pdf). It is not solar-specific and was not saved.

The consumption-linked capacity rule (capacity limited to the previous 12 months' average consumption) is real but appears to have NO published instrument. Press reports say MSEDCL implemented it in its RTS application portal from about 13 Feb 2026. Installers are quoted: "There is no notice or any circular from MSEDCL" (jwrsolar.in). The Hitavada (16 Feb 2026) reports that AIREA wrote to MNRE saying it had not seen any MERC notification of the change. No such circular appears on mahadiscom.in (commercial circulars, I-SMART guidelines list). The claimed number MSEDCL/COMM/RTS/2025/18 (10.01.2025) and the 1,400 kWh/kW formula are fabricated. Nearest real but different instrument: ED(Infra)/RTS/No. 00786 dt 07.01.2025, "Guidelines for observing PV capacity (AC/DC) installed in accordance with Connected/Sanctioned Load of prosumer for RTS installations" (https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/media/PV_CAPACITY_INVERTER_GUIDELINES.pdf). It ties capacity to sanctioned load, not consumption, so it was not saved.

No MEDA/MAHAURJA guideline on rooftop vendor empanelment or non-subsidy rooftop registrations was found on mahaurja.com (solar pages list only GCRT 2017-19 beneficiary lists, benchmark costs, Kusum, and similar items). Under PM Surya Ghar, vendor registration in Maharashtra is done by the DISCOM, not MEDA. The real instruments are both MSEDCL, so the issuer differs from the claim and they were not saved under this MEDA doc_id. (1) CE(SPD)/RTS/PBG/21576 dt 12.07.2024, "Empanelment of vendors under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana": vendors register with the DISCOM and deposit a PBG of Rs 2,50,000 valid at least five years (https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/media/Empanelment%20of%20vendors%20under%20PMSuryaghar%20MBY.pdf). (2) ED(Infra)/RTS/No. 7125 dt 03.03.2025, "Go live of RTS Vendor Portal Version-2 for Non-Subsidized Scheme" (https://www.mahadiscom.in/ismart/media/RTS_VENDOR_PORTAL_NON-SUBSIDY_03.03.2025.pdf). The researcher may reassign one of these under an MSEDCL (C5) doc_id.
